RECOVERIQ — COMPLETE CLAUDE VERIFICATION REPORT
==============================================================================================================



PURPOSE
-------

Audit the CURRENT RecoverIQ repository up to the pre-final-training checkpoint.

Do not modify the repository while performing the first audit.

For each subsystem classify it:

    PASS
    WARNING
    FAIL

For each WARNING or FAIL provide:

    exact file
    exact function/class
    exact reason
    minimal fix

IMPORTANT ARCHITECTURAL DISTINCTION

There are TWO separate ML concepts:

1. Late-payment model

   At invoice posting time:

       "How likely is this B2B invoice to be paid late?"

   Output:
       late_payment_probability

   Target:
       late_payment_weekend_adjusted

2. Existing recovery-risk model

   Used later for overdue/recovery workflows.

   Output includes:
       recovery_probability
       risk_score
       risk_level

These must remain separate.

CURRENT CHECKPOINT

Expected to be wired:

    shared 22-feature late-payment contract
    PostgreSQL runtime feature builder
    RF / GB / XGBoost runtime loader
    SHAP layer
    persistence fields
    POST /invoices
    seed fields
    LangGraph context
    existing policy/review system

Expected NOT to be finished:

    fresh final RF retraining
    fresh final GB retraining
    fresh final XGBoost retraining
    final runtime_contract packaging
    model activation
    final end-to-end live inference
    final untouched-test evaluation

Existing model reports may be STALE.
Do not treat them as final performance.

SECRETS POLICY

.env and environment secrets are intentionally excluded from this report.

 ==========================

 Python was created in the early 1990s by Guido van Rossum at Stichting
 Mathematisch Centrum (CWI, see https://www.cwi.nl) in the Netherlands
 as a successor of a language called ABC.  Guido remains Python's
 principal author, although it includes many contributions from others.

 In 1995, Guido continued his work on Python at the Corporation for
 National Research Initiatives (CNRI, see https://www.cnri.reston.va.us)
 in Reston, Virginia where he released several versions of the
 software.

 In May 2000, Guido and the Python core development team moved to
 BeOpen.com to form the BeOpen PythonLabs team.  In October of the same
 year, the PythonLabs team moved to Digital Creations, which became
 Zope Corporation.  In 2001, the Python Software Foundation (PSF, see
 https://www.python.org/psf/) was formed, a non-profit organization
 created specifically to own Python-related Intellectual Property.
 Zope Corporation was a sponsoring member of the PSF.

 All Python releases are Open Source (see https://opensource.org for
 the Open Source Definition).  Historically, most, but not all, Python
 releases have also been GPL-compatible; the table below summarizes
 the various releases.

     Release         Derived     Year        Owner       GPL-
                     from                                compatible? (1)

     0.9.0 thru 1.2              1991-1995   CWI         yes
     1.3 thru 1.5.2  1.2         1995-1999   CNRI        yes
     1.6             1.5.2       2000        CNRI        no
     2.0             1.6         2000        BeOpen.com  no
     1.6.1           1.6         2001        CNRI        yes (2)
     2.1             2.0+1.6.1   2001        PSF         no

prepare_categorical source:
def prepare_categorical(
    frames: list[pd.DataFrame],
) -> list[pd.DataFrame]:
    """Prepare native categorical features using train-only vocabulary.

    The first frame must be the training frame. Category levels are learned
    only from it. Unseen categories in later frames become missing values
    rather than leaking future category vocabulary into training.
    """
    if not frames:
        return []

    train_frame = frames[0]

    category_levels = {
        column: sorted(
            train_frame[column]
            .dropna()
            .astype(str)
            .unique()
            .tolist()
        )
        for column in MODEL_CATEGORICAL_FEATURES
    }

    prepared: list[pd.DataFrame] = []

    for frame in frames:
        X = frame[FEATURES].copy()

        for column in MODEL_CATEGORICAL_FEATURES:
            values = frame[column].astype("string")

            X[column] = pd.Categorical(
                values,
                categories=category_levels[column],
            )

        prepared.append(X)

    return prepared


to_numeric_codes source:
def to_numeric_codes(frames: list[pd.DataFrame], medians: pd.Series | None = None):
    """Integer-code the categoricals and median-fill NaNs.

    For scikit-learn estimators, which have neither native categorical
    support nor native NaN handling. The medians come from TRAIN only and
    are returned so they can be saved alongside the model: the saved
    estimator is unusable without them, because scoring a raw frame against
    it silently produces wrong answers rather than an error.
    """
    coded = []
    for frame in frames:
        X = frame.copy()
        for column in MODEL_CATEGORICAL_FEATURES:
            X[column] = X[column].cat.codes
        coded.append(X)
    if medians is None:
        medians = coded[0].median()
    return [X.fillna(medians) for X in coded], medians

  best calibration     xgboost              0.5320 log loss
  best worst-fold      gradient_boosting    0.4217
  least overfit        random_forest        +0.124 gap

  No model wins on every criterion, so the choice depends on the job:
    ranking which invoices to chase first  -> optimise ROC/PR-AUC
    a probability you will quote or threshold -> optimise log loss
    surviving a change in payment behaviour   -> optimise worst-fold

  BUT none of these models is stable across time, and the worst-fold
  column is the honest summary of that: every one of them ranks
  backwards in at least one period. No validation figure here should
  be quoted as expected performance.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass

TARGET_COLUMN = "late_payment_weekend_adjusted"

NUMERIC_FEATURES = [
    "amount",
    "payment_term",
    "prior_resolved_invoice_count",
    "prior_open_invoice_count",
    "open_invoice_ratio",
    "has_resolved_history",
    "historical_late_rate",
    "historical_avg_days_late",
    "historical_avg_invoice_amount",
    "amount_vs_historical_avg_ratio",
    "customer_tenure_days",
    "days_since_previous_invoice",
    "recent_5_late_rate",
    "recent_5_avg_days_late",
    "recent_late_streak",
    "recent_on_time_streak",
    "recent_5_late_rate_delta",
    "recent_5_avg_days_late_delta",
]

CATEGORICAL_FEATURES = [
    "payment_method_description",
    "region",
    "city",
    "zipcode",
]

FEATURES = NUMERIC_FEATURES + CATEGORICAL_FEATURES


@dataclass(slots=True)
class PaymentRiskFeatures:
    amount: float
    payment_term: float

    prior_resolved_invoice_count: float
    prior_open_invoice_count: float
    open_invoice_ratio: float
    has_resolved_history: float

    historical_late_rate: float
    historical_avg_days_late: float

    historical_avg_invoice_amount: float
    amount_vs_historical_avg_ratio: float

    customer_tenure_days: float
    days_since_previous_invoice: float

    recent_5_late_rate: float
    recent_5_avg_days_late: float

    recent_late_streak: float
    recent_on_time_streak: float

    recent_5_late_rate_delta: float
    recent_5_avg_days_late_delta: float

    payment_method_description: str
    region: str
    city: str
    zipcode: str

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, float | str]:
        return asdict(self)

    def to_row(self) -> dict[str, float | str]:
        values = self.to_dict()
        return {feature: values[feature] for feature in FEATURES}


assert list(PaymentRiskFeatures.__dataclass_fields__) == FEATURES

"""Shared evaluation core for the RecoverIQ late-payment models.

The three trainers — train_xgboost.py, train_random_forest.py,
train_gradient_boosting.py — each own their model and nothing else. Data
loading, the metric definitions, the fold construction and the stability
check all live here, imported by all three.

That split is deliberate. The six scripts this replaced each carried their
own copy of the split loading and scoring, drifted apart, and ended up
reporting numbers that were not comparable with one another: one trained
on late_payment_strict while the pipeline declared
late_payment_weekend_adjusted canonical, and the committed metrics had
been generated by a still older version. A comparison table is only worth
reading if every row was produced by the same code.

WHY THE HEADLINE METRIC IS WITHIN-PERIOD AUC
--------------------------------------------
The late rate moves hard across the validation window:

    2015-10   63.2%
    2015-11   39.0%
    2015-12   29.7%

Pooled ROC-AUC over a window like that conflates two questions — "is this
invoice riskier than that one" and "is this month riskier than that
month" — and a model with no access to the period cannot answer the
second. The effect is big enough to invert the metric: one run scored
0.5481 pooled while every individual month inside it scored 0.57-0.61. A
pooled figure below every one of its own components is measuring drift,
not skill.

So within_period_auc ranks invoices only against others posted in the
same month, weighted by month size. pooled_roc_auc is still reported,
because omitting it would be its own kind of dishonesty, but it is not
what models are selected on.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.metrics import (
    accuracy_score,
    average_precision_score,
    brier_score_loss,
    f1_score,
    log_loss,
    precision_score,
    recall_score,
    roc_auc_score,
)

from app.ml.payment_features import (
    CATEGORICAL_FEATURES as MODEL_CATEGORICAL_FEATURES,
    NUMERIC_FEATURES as MODEL_NUMERIC_FEATURES,
    TARGET_COLUMN,
)

PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
SPLIT_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT / "data" / "processed" / "primary" / "splits"
ARTIFACT_ROOT = Path(__file__).parent / "artifacts" / "models"

RANDOM_STATE = 42

# Rows with less history than this are excluded from a fold's score. The
# causal history features need accumulated history, so the earliest fold
# has almost none; the previous selection score averaged those near-chance
# folds in and came out anti-correlated with validation, actively
# preferring the models that used history worst.
MIN_HISTORY_FOR_SCORING = 3

FEATURES = MODEL_NUMERIC_FEATURES + MODEL_CATEGORICAL_FEATURES


def load(name: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    path = SPLIT_DIR / f"{name}.csv.gz"
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"{path} not found. Run `python -m app.ml.datasets.build_primary_features` "
            "then `python -m app.ml.datasets.create_primary_splits` first."
        )
    return pd.read_csv(path, parse_dates=["doc_date", "posting_date", "net_due_date"])


def load_splits() -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """train, validation, test. Test is returned so category levels can be
    aligned across all three; no trainer may read its target."""
    return load("train"), load("validation"), load("test")


def prepare_categorical(
    frames: list[pd.DataFrame],
) -> list[pd.DataFrame]:
    """Prepare native categorical features using train-only vocabulary.

    The first frame must be the training frame. Category levels are learned
    only from it. Unseen categories in later frames become missing values
    rather than leaking future category vocabulary into training.
    """
    if not frames:
        return []

    train_frame = frames[0]

    category_levels = {
        column: sorted(
            train_frame[column]
            .dropna()
            .astype(str)
            .unique()
            .tolist()
        )
        for column in MODEL_CATEGORICAL_FEATURES
    }

    prepared: list[pd.DataFrame] = []

    for frame in frames:
        X = frame[FEATURES].copy()

        for column in MODEL_CATEGORICAL_FEATURES:
            values = frame[column].astype("string")

            X[column] = pd.Categorical(
                values,
                categories=category_levels[column],
            )

        prepared.append(X)

    return prepared


def to_numeric_codes(frames: list[pd.DataFrame], medians: pd.Series | None = None):
    """Integer-code the categoricals and median-fill NaNs.

    For scikit-learn estimators, which have neither native categorical
    support nor native NaN handling. The medians come from TRAIN only and
    are returned so they can be saved alongside the model: the saved
    estimator is unusable without them, because scoring a raw frame against
    it silently produces wrong answers rather than an error.
    """
    coded = []
    for frame in frames:
        X = frame.copy()
        for column in MODEL_CATEGORICAL_FEATURES:
            X[column] = X[column].cat.codes
        coded.append(X)
    if medians is None:
        medians = coded[0].median()
    return [X.fillna(medians) for X in coded], medians


def within_period_auc(frame: pd.DataFrame, probabilities: np.ndarray) -> tuple[float, dict]:
    months = frame["posting_date"].dt.to_period("M")
    scores, weights, per_month = [], [], {}
    for month in months.unique():
        mask = (months == month).to_numpy()
        y = frame.loc[mask, TARGET_COLUMN]
        if y.nunique() < 2:
            continue
        auc = float(roc_auc_score(y, probabilities[mask]))
        per_month[str(month)] = {
            "rows": int(mask.sum()),
            "late_rate": round(float(y.mean()), 4),
            "auc": round(auc, 4),
        }
        scores.append(auc)
        weights.append(int(mask.sum()))
    if not scores:
        return float("nan"), {}
    return float(np.average(scores, weights=weights)), per_month


def evaluate(frame: pd.DataFrame, probabilities: np.ndarray, threshold: float = 0.5) -> dict:
    y = frame[TARGET_COLUMN]
    predicted = (probabilities >= threshold).astype(int)
    weighted, per_month = within_period_auc(frame, probabilities)
    return {
        "within_period_auc": round(weighted, 4),
        "pooled_roc_auc": round(float(roc_auc_score(y, probabilities)), 4),
        "pooled_pr_auc": round(float(average_precision_score(y, probabilities)), 4),
        "log_loss": round(float(log_loss(y, probabilities)), 4),
        "brier": round(float(brier_score_loss(y, probabilities)), 4),
        "accuracy": round(float(accuracy_score(y, predicted)), 4),
        "precision": round(float(precision_score(y, predicted, zero_division=0)), 4),
        "recall": round(float(recall_score(y, predicted, zero_division=0)), 4),
        "f1": round(float(f1_score(y, predicted, zero_division=0)), 4),
        "per_month": per_month,
    }


def temporal_folds(frame: pd.DataFrame, n_folds: int = 4) -> list[tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]]:
    """Expanding-window folds on whole posting dates."""
    daily = frame.groupby("posting_date", sort=True).size().cumsum()
    fractions = np.linspace(0.40, 1.00, n_folds + 1)
    cutoffs = [
        daily.index[int(np.argmin(np.abs(daily.to_numpy() - fraction * len(frame))))]
        for fraction in fractions
    ]
    folds = []
    for index in range(n_folds):
        train_mask = frame["posting_date"] <= cutoffs[index]
        test_mask = (frame["posting_date"] > cutoffs[index]) & (
            frame["posting_date"] <= cutoffs[index + 1]
        )
        if test_mask.sum() == 0 or frame.loc[train_mask, TARGET_COLUMN].nunique() < 2:
            continue
        folds.append(
            (np.flatnonzero(train_mask.to_numpy()), np.flatnonzero(test_mask.to_numpy()))
        )
    return folds


def stability_report(fold_aucs: list[float], fold_base_rates: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """Does this model hold up across time, or is one good window luck?

    A fold below 0.50 means the ranking is REVERSED in that period, which
    is worse than having no model. Every candidate configuration tested so
    far inverts on the same fold, so this is a property of the data rather
    than of any one model's hyperparameters — which is precisely why it
    belongs in every model's report and not in a footnote.
    """
    if not fold_aucs:
        return {"stable": False, "reason": "no scoreable folds"}
    inverted = [round(a, 4) for a in fold_aucs if a < 0.50]
    return {
        "fold_aucs": [round(a, 4) for a in fold_aucs],
        "mean": round(float(np.mean(fold_aucs)), 4),
        "min": round(float(np.min(fold_aucs)), 4),
        "max": round(float(np.max(fold_aucs)), 4),
        "std": round(float(np.std(fold_aucs)), 4),
        "inverted_folds": inverted,
        "fold_base_rates": fold_base_rates,
        "stable": not inverted and float(np.std(fold_aucs)) < 0.10,
    }


def print_stability(stability: dict) -> None:
    print()
    print("  STABILITY VERDICT")
    if stability.get("stable"):
        print("    stable: fold scores agree and none invert.")
        return
    print("    NOT STABLE. This is the headline finding, not a footnote.")
    inverted = stability.get("inverted_folds") or []
    if inverted:
        print(f"    {len(inverted)} fold(s) scored BELOW 0.50 ({inverted}) — the ranking")
        print("    is reversed in those periods, which is worse than no model at all.")
    print(f"    fold std {stability['std']:.4f} across {stability['min']:.4f}-{stability['max']:.4f}.")
    print()
    print("    Cause: the late rate shifts between adjacent five-week windows, so a")
    print("    model calibrated on one regime ranks backwards in the next:")
    for number, rates in enumerate(stability.get("fold_base_rates", [])):
        print(f"      fold {number}: train late {rates['train_late_rate']:.4f}"
              f"  ->  test late {rates['test_late_rate']:.4f}")
    print()
    print("    That is a process-level regime change in when payment runs fire, not")
    print("    invoice-level credit risk. The validation figure is one window that")
    print("    resembled its training period and must NOT be quoted as expected")
    print("    performance.")


def fold_base_rates(frame: pd.DataFrame, folds) -> list[dict]:
    return [
        {
            "train_late_rate": round(float(frame[TARGET_COLUMN].iloc[tr].mean()), 4),
            "test_late_rate": round(float(frame[TARGET_COLUMN].iloc[te].mean()), 4),
        }
        for tr, te in folds
    ]


def baselines(train: pd.DataFrame, validation: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
    """What any model has to beat to be worth having.

    A constant at the base rate, and the customer's own historical late
    rate. The second is the one that matters: if a model cannot beat a
    per-customer lookup table, it is a lookup table with extra steps.
    """
    base_rate = float(train[TARGET_COLUMN].mean())
    history = train.groupby("cust_num")[TARGET_COLUMN].mean()
    return {
        "constant_base_rate": evaluate(
            validation, np.full(len(validation), base_rate)
        ),
        "customer_history": evaluate(
            validation,
            validation["cust_num"].map(history).fillna(base_rate).to_numpy(),
        ),
    }


def print_data_summary(train, validation, test, model_name: str) -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print(f"{model_name.upper()}  —  RecoverIQ late-payment model")
    print("=" * 78)
    print(f"  train      {len(train):>6} rows  {train.posting_date.min().date()} -> "
          f"{train.posting_date.max().date()}  late {train[TARGET_COLUMN].mean():.4f}")
    print(f"  validation {len(validation):>6} rows  {validation.posting_date.min().date()} -> "
          f"{validation.posting_date.max().date()}  late {validation[TARGET_COLUMN].mean():.4f}")
    print(f"  test       {len(test):>6} rows  RESERVED, not read")
    print(f"  features   {len(MODEL_NUMERIC_FEATURES)} numeric + "
          f"{len(MODEL_CATEGORICAL_FEATURES)} categorical")
    print(f"  target     {TARGET_COLUMN}")


def write_report(model_slug: str, report: dict) -> Path:
    directory = ARTIFACT_ROOT / model_slug
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = directory / "report.json"
    path.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
    return path


def print_comparison_row_header() -> None:
    print(f"  {'model':<28} {'within':>8} {'pooled':>8} {'logloss':>9} {'brier':>8}")
    print("  " + "-" * 64)


def print_comparison_row(name: str, scored: dict) -> None:
    print(f"  {name:<28} {scored['within_period_auc']:>8.4f} "
          f"{scored['pooled_roc_auc']:>8.4f} {scored['log_loss']:>9.4f} "
          f"{scored['brier']:>8.4f}")

"""Build RecoverIQ primary B2B features - V3.

V2 changes
----------
1. Preserve the original strict lateness outcome for auditing.
2. Create a weekend-adjusted late-payment target:
      Saturday due date -> following Monday
      Sunday due date   -> following Monday
   Holidays are NOT adjusted because the source does not provide
   enough geography/calendar information to do that reliably.
3. Remove posting_weekday and due_weekday from model inputs.
4. Add richer causal customer-history features.
5. Add recent 3/5/10 resolved-invoice behaviour.
6. Add behavioural trend and workload features.
7. Preserve the rule that an invoice outcome is usable only if its
   clearing date was known BEFORE the current invoice posting date.

Raw source
----------
data/raw/b2b_primary/b2b_invoice_payment_45839.csv
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import deque
import heapq
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from app.ml.payment_features import (
    CATEGORICAL_FEATURES as SHARED_CATEGORICAL_FEATURES,
    NUMERIC_FEATURES as SHARED_NUMERIC_FEATURES,
    TARGET_COLUMN as SHARED_TARGET_COLUMN,
)


PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]

RAW_PATH = (
    PROJECT_ROOT
    / "data"
    / "raw"
    / "b2b_primary"
    / "b2b_invoice_payment_45839.csv"
)

PROCESSED_DIR = (
    PROJECT_ROOT
    / "data"
    / "processed"
    / "primary"
)

OUTPUT_PATH = (
    PROCESSED_DIR
    / "b2b_primary_features.csv.gz"
)

MANIFEST_PATH = (
    PROCESSED_DIR
    / "b2b_primary_features_manifest.json"
)


STRICT_TARGET_COLUMN = "late_payment_strict"

TARGET_COLUMN = SHARED_TARGET_COLUMN


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# V3: OBSERVATION HORIZON (right-censoring fix)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# The raw extract only contains invoices that had CLEARED by its last
# clearing date (2016-03-17). Any invoice still unpaid on that date is
# absent from the file entirely -- and those are precisely the slowest
# payers. The effect compounds the later an invoice was posted, which
# silently destroyed the comparability of the splits:
#
#     split        mean resolution    p95      MAX
#     train            18.4 d         98 d    1437 d
#     validation        7.4 d         35 d     104 d
#     test              5.1 d          9 d      22 d
#
# The test partition could not contain an invoice that took longer than
# three weeks to clear. It was structurally incapable of holding the
# cases this project exists to find, so every number measured on it was
# optimistic for a reason no model change could fix.
#
# Fix: keep an invoice only when its due date leaves a full horizon of
# observation before the extract ends:
#
#     net_due_date + OBSERVATION_HORIZON_DAYS <= data cutoff
#
# Within the retained set, a late payer is as visible as a prompt one,
# so train / validation / test are drawn from one population again.
#
# Choosing 45 days, measured rather than guessed. On invoices with at
# least a 200-day observation window (where the distribution is
# unbiased), the share of late payments that resolve within H days of
# the due date is:
#
#     H= 7d  87.4%      H= 45d  96.8%
#     H=14d  93.2%      H= 60d  98.9%
#     H=30d  94.0%      H= 90d  99.0%
#
# and the share of rows retained is 95.7% at H=30, 91.2% at H=45,
# 86.1% at H=60. H=45 observes ~97% of late outcomes while keeping
# ~91% of the data.
#
# Residual limitation, stated rather than hidden: an invoice that runs
# more than 45 days past due AND is due within 45 days of the cutoff is
# still unobservable. That is ~3% of late cases in the tail, not the
# systematic, split-correlated bias that was there before.
OBSERVATION_HORIZON_DAYS = 45


LEAKAGE_COLUMNS = [
    "clearing_doc",
    "clearing_date",
    "days_overdue_delay",
    "delay_bins",
    "weekday_clearing",
    "quarter_clearing",
    "weekday_clearnum",
    "delayflag",
]


UNSAFE_PRECOMPUTED_COLUMNS = [

    "rank_of_order_by_customer",
    "age_of_customer_months",
    "age_of_customer_year",
    "customer_age_year_bins",
